faq.a: It is charcoal heated with steam or chemicals so it becomes full of tiny pores. One gram can have an inner surface of hundreds of square metres, which grabs chemicals from water.
asks: Why are water filters black inside?

faq.q: How does a water filter jug work?
faq.a: Water seeps slowly through a cartridge of activated carbon, which traps taste-causing chemicals like chlorine, and resin beads, which remove some of the calcium that makes limescale.
asks: What is inside a Brita filter?

faq.q: Does a filter jug kill germs?
faq.a: No. Jug filters improve the taste of water that is already safe. They do not make unsafe water drinkable; that needs boiling or special purifiers.
asks: Can I filter dirty water with a filter jug?

faq.q: Why does filtered water make less limescale?
faq.a: Hard water has dissolved calcium. The resin beads swap calcium for other ions, so less of it is left to form scale in your kettle.

faq.q: Why must the cartridge be changed?
faq.a: The carbon surface and the resin slowly fill up, so after a few weeks they stop working and can even let trapped things back out. Most makers suggest about every four weeks.
asks: How often should I change a water filter?

facts: A single gram of activated carbon can have an internal surface area of several hundred square metres.
Filter jugs improve the taste of safe tap water but are not designed to make unsafe water drinkable.
